name.description: Deprecated: the name is metadata.name, as Kubernetes keeps it. Read from a manifest saved before 2.6.0 and folded into metadata.name; never written.

category.description: What form the source takes. Who runs it is provenance, a separate question (DCAT keeps the dataset, its distribution and its publisher apart).

provenance.description: Whether the organisation runs this source or a third party does. Older files that used the category externalThirdParty are rewritten on read to provenance external.

capture.description: How each record gets into this source. A source filled from paper has to say how the paper becomes data, because that decides how soon anything read from it can be known: an assessment printed for hand marking cannot report in weeks. notDecided is an honest answer and is advised wherever a time-bound target reads from here. See TAXONOMY.md D18.

classification.description: Information classification from a fixed scheme (ISO/IEC 27002:2022, 5.12 and 5.13: classify by a labelled scheme). Older free-text values that match a level are rewritten on read; any other value is dropped with a note, since guessing a classification is worse than leaving it unset.
